newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABARE sees Australia nickel output 72,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: ABARE sees Australia nickel output 72,000 tonnes.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday Australia remained on track to produce about 72,000 tonnes of refined nickel in 1997/98 (July/June).
The forecast, contained in ABARE's latest Australian Commodities quarterly, is unchanged from the previous estimate made in March and up 7.2 percent from its 1996/97 estimate.
ABARE said the Australian nickel industry has entered a period of rapid growth.
Australian nickel mine production is forecast to rise by 15 percent in 1997/98, following an estimated increase of 8.5 percent in 1996/97.
The value of Australian nickel exports, which fell about two percent in 1996/97 because of lower world prices, should increase by nearly 30 percent to A$1.5 billion in 1997/98, ABARE said.

ABARE said it expected world nickel prices based on the average at the London Metal Exchange to rise five percent in calendar 1997 to US$7,850 a tonne ($3.56 a pound) and 15 percent in 1998 to $9,000 a tonne ($4.08).
The higher prices reflect a forecast six percent rise in global demand for nickel in 1997, followed by 3.3 percent rise in 1998, ABARE said.

Higher forecast growth in nickel consumption is underpinned by expected recoveries in stainless steel output in 1997 and further gains in 1998 as steelmakers respond to strong demand associated with expanding world economic activity, it said.
World production of primary nickel is forecast to increase 3.2 percent to 979,000 tonnes in 1997 and to rise at a similar rate to one million tonnes in 1998, ABARE said.
Expectations that demand will outpace production in 1997 and 1998 should reduce inventory levels.

"Combined LME and producer stocks are forecast to fall from the equivalent of 8.9 weeks of consumption at the end of 1996 to 7.8 weeks of consumption by the end of 1997 and 6.7 weeks of consumption at the end of 1998, a level not seen since 1988," it said.
